questions.title: Stable Order of Contest Results
questions.description:
Contestants finished with possibly equal scores. The rules require a STABLE ordering: equal scores keep the arrival order. You receive the scores (line 2) and arrival ids (line 3, aligned by position); return the ids ordered by stable ascending score. Implement the stable sort yourself, e.g. insertion sort on pairs — std::sort and std::stable_sort are banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> stable_ids(const std::vector<int> &scores, const std::vector<int> &ids)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated scores. Line 3: n distinct space-separated ids.

Output Format:
One line with the ids in stable score order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= scores <= 1000000, ids distinct

You receive prices (line 2) and ids (line 3, aligned by position); return the ids in final rank order. Implement the sort manually — std::sort is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

    std::vector<int> rank_products(const std::vector<int> &prices, const std::vector<int> &ids)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated prices. Line 3: n distinct space-separated ids.

Output Format:
One line with the ids in rank order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= prices <= 1000000, ids distinct

questions.title: Shelf by Popularity Then Label
questions.description:
A library shelf reorders books by popularity: values that occur more often come first, and equally popular values are ordered by the value itself ascending. n is small, so you may recount a value's frequency with a scan whenever needed. No library sort — order the vector manually. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> freq_order(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the values ordered by (frequency descending, value ascending). The harness prints them space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated values.

Output Format:
One line with the ordered values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Bubble Sort a Vector
questions.description:
Implement the classic bubble sort: repeatedly step through the vector, swapping adjacent elements that are out of order, until everything is ascending. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> bubble_sort(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the vector sorted ascending. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Selection Sort a Vector
questions.description:

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> selection_sort(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the vector sorted ascending. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Roster After k Bubble Passes
questions.description:
A duty roster is being sorted by bubble sort while the supervisor watches. Predict the state after EXACTLY k passes, where one pass is a full left-to-right scan (j from 0 to n-2) swapping adjacent out-of-order pairs. k may exceed the number of passes actually needed — extra passes leave a sorted roster unchanged. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> bubble_after_k(std::vector<int> v, int k)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the roster after exactly k passes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k <= 1000

Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> selection_after_k(std::vector<int> v, int k)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the standings after exactly k passes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k <= 1000

questions.title: Comparisons for Early-Stop Bubble
questions.description:
Bubble sort can stop early: pass over the array (full scans, j from 0 to n-2, one comparison per adjacent check) and stop after the first pass that performs NO swaps. Count the total number of adjacent comparisons performed — a sorted input costs exactly n-1. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int bubble_comparisons(std::vector<int> v)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the total comparison count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
